newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton prices gain ahead of transport strike.
newsitem.headline: India cotton prices gain ahead of transport strike.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Monday gained as a transport strike on April 1 loomed ahead, dealers said.
Limited arrivals due to the proposed strike called by transporters dragged prices up while millers remained average buyers.
Transport operators in India are protesting against a service tax and hike in the insurance premiums.
"The strike has curtailed supplies of cotton while millers remain active buyers to cover positions ahead of any shortage in the coming days if strike continues," one broker said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 20/30 rupees at 900/940 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned looked up by 20 rupees at 1,520/1,650 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Sankar Kalyan (medium-staple) lifted by 200 rupees at 13,200/13,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
Overall market sentiments remained firm at the close of the session. -- Bombay Commodities +91-22-265 9000
